LESSON: RHYTHM

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.3: Rhythm
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rhythm, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How are rhythmic patterns created? 2. How can rhythm be used in daily life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. interpret rhythmic patterns involving minim, crotchet a pair of quavers and their rests,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. create rhythms using music note values and their rests,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. make a calligraphy pen for writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. write in calligraphy French rhythm names of a rhythmic pattern,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. aurally identify rhythm in two-beat patterns,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. compose simple rhythms in two-beat patterns,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

G. enjoy creating rhythms using music notes and their rests.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. interpret rhythmic patterns involving minim, crotchet a pair of quavers and their rests,

   Rhythm helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. create rhythms using music note values and their rests,

   Rhythm helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. make a calligraphy pen for writing,

   Rhythm helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. write in calligraphy French rhythm names of a rhythmic pattern,

   Rhythm helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. aurally identify rhythm in two-beat patterns,

   Rhythm helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. compose simple rhythms in two-beat patterns,

   Rhythm helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

G. enjoy creating rhythms using music notes and their rests.

   Rhythm helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

H. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to/sing simple songs involving minim, crotchet, pair of quavers and their rests and clap/tap their rhythmic patterns, Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communications.  relate the French rhythm names to music note symbols and their rests,

2. practice writing the note symbols of a minim, crotchet, a pair of quavers and their rests on monotone, Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to/sing simple songs involving minim, crotchet, pair of quavers and their rests and clap/tap their rhythmic patterns, Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communications.  relate the French rhythm names to music note symbols and their rests,
2. practice writing the note symbols of a minim, crotchet, a pair of quavers and their rests on monotone, Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rhythm together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: developed as a learner works with a peer to execute a cartwheel and when they speak

clearly to provide feedback on peers’ composed rhythmic patterns.

● Creativity and imagination: developed as the learner utilises the composition techniques to compose original rhythmic

patterns in two-beat patterns.

● Learning to learn: developed as the learner takes initiative to understand how rhythmic patterns are created.
